question.text: Jeevan Jyoti Foundation runs a charitable hospital in rural Maharashtra. Its annual receipts are INR 4.5 crore. The SIA is advising the board on the cleanest tax-exemption route. Under which provision can a charitable hospital claim exemption as a 'specified institution' subject to prescribed receipt limits, distinct from the Section 11 general charitable-trust route?

answer.text: Section 10(23C) — specified educational and medical institutions, subject to prescribed receipt thresholds
Section 80G — the institution itself becomes tax-exempt under 80G registration
Section 115BBI — exemption for anonymous donations above INR 1 lakh
Section 2(15) — exemption applies to any entity with a 'charitable purpose'

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10(23C) of the Income Tax Act provides an exemption route for specified institutions — notably educational institutions and hospitals that exist solely for philanthropic purposes and not for profit — subject to prescribed receipt limits and approval from the prescribed authority. This sits parallel to the general charitable-trust exemption available under Section 11/12AB. The other listed provisions serve different functions: Section 80G is a donor-side deduction; Section 115BBI is an anti-abuse rate on anonymous donations; Section 2(15) merely defines the term "charitable purpose". The Trap: Section 80G gives the donor a deduction; it does not make the institution tax-exempt. Section 115BBI is a penalty charge on anonymous donations rather than an exemption. Section 2(15) is definitional and on its own confers no exemption. Note: The Social Impact Assessors workbook discusses Section 12AB, Section 80G, Section 11, and Section 2(15) on the cited pages but does not, on those pages, set out the Section 10(23C) specified-institution exemption route or its receipt-limit conditions. That framing is drawn from Section 10(23C) of the Income Tax Act rather than from the workbook pages checked.
